program_terms.location: Programme page, 'Monto Mínimo'

program_terms.notes: Restates DE 722 of 2020 art. 3 (t-fce91dcfaf, recorded in PAB). The page prints '$' and, in the same sentence, 'USD $', so the currency is recorded as USD as printed (balboa at par with the US dollar); not linked automatically to the PAB rows because the currency differs. The page does not say whether the $500,000 is the overall minimum or the real estate minimum; 'libre de gravámenes' and '(en lugar de USD $500,000)' point to real estate. Undated page; no validity stated for this amount.

ledger.contains: MICI release on DE 17 of 2026 at the groundbreaking of a Mercan Group residential project. Already in the tables: 268 certificates / B/.113.6 million (Jul 2025-Jun 2026), 193 / over B/.90.1 million (previous period), real estate 87.3% of certificates. DE 17 amounts already in program_terms from the gazette. Out of scope: the Mercan Group project (48-storey tower, 200 apartments, delivery 2028, Mercan plan of about B/.200 million), which the release does not say is a qualifying project or count of programme investment. Nothing new added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Undated MICI programme page for DE 722 (titled 'Decreto ejecutivo 722-antes'): purpose, investment forms, minimums ($500,000 free of liens; USD 300,000 real estate under DE 109 of 2022 until 15 Oct 2024; $500,000 securities; USD 750,000 fixed deposit), benefits (permanent residence, filing before entry, approval in 30 working days, SNM special window). All these rules are already in program_terms from the decrees (DE 722, DE 109, DE 193); the 30 working days is a legal maximum, already t-a422c5cd9e. No statistics. Nothing new added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

SNM residence permits 2025 (preliminary to 31 Dec 2025): Cuadro 1 by month, Cuadro 2 by type, Cuadro 3 by sex, Cuadro 4 by category (decided/approved/denied), Cuadro 5 by country (all categories), Cuadro 6 by age and sex, plus charts. In scope: Cuadro 4 rows PAISES AMIGOS, INVERSIONISTA CALIFICADO, SOLVENCIA PROPIA deposit and real estate (12 rows, all already in the tables). Cuadro 4 checked: categories add up to 35,017 / 33,262 / 1,755 and approved + denied = total on every row. No other investor category printed separately. Other tables cover all permits (out of scope). Nothing new added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

COA annual audit report on PRA for 2023 and 2022 (187 pp.): executive summary (officers, manpower, financial highlights, budget vs actual, bases of qualified opinion, other observations), auditor report, management statement (image), financial statements and notes, Part II financial observations (trust liabilities and PRA's share of interest on members' deposits with Table 2, deferred tax, cash, APF accruals, receivables, Table 9 deposits per private bank PRA vs bank records, withholding tax, ECL, payables, leases, after-enrolment service fees held for BI, restricted funds) and non-financial observations (marketing: AP&M expenses Table 21, PRA top markets Table 22, spending by market Table 23, budget and enrollees Table 24, expense and enrollees by country Table 25, survey Table 26, walk-in vs marketer by office; internet services; website project; visa application process and BI fees), Part III prior recommendations, Annex A. Taken: income, fees by type (2022 restated), interest and PRA interest share, costs, net income, budget, staff, marketers and enrolments via marketers, deposits (restricted funds, trust liabilities, interest due, per-bank deposits in Table 9), BI fees paid, processing times, enrolment target and counts, marketing budgets and spending (Tables 21, 23, 24, 25), principals by nationality (Tables 22, 25), walk-in/marketer by office, Austrian members, events. Not taken (out of scope): Table 26 survey of how members learned of the SRRV (1,524 responses), after-enrolment services (1,680 retirees; P2.644 million BI fees held), reconciliation variances, misstatement amounts, receivables, deferred tax, leases, internet and website contracts, number of cancelled cheques. Checks: Note 24.1 and 25 lines add up; Table 21 adds up; Table 23 total (P66,023,820) differs from Table 21 total (P65,648,789); Table 22 has no total; the Table 24 last column header is ambiguous (read as 2022). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Philippine Consulate General New York page on the Special Investor's Resident Visa: indefinite residence while the investment subsists; eligibility (age 21+, healthy, no derogatory record, US$75,000 in a listed company, IPP project or manufacturing/services firm; spouse and children under 21), privileges (duty-free household goods), documents, deposit via LBP or DBP, fees (US$500 filing, US$25 notarization per document per copy, courier), 20-day processing at the consulate, BOI One-Stop SIRV Center evaluation, probationary six-month SIRV. Rest of the page is consulate navigation and news. No statistics. All programme amounts and periods are now in the data (investment and filing fee were already there). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

PRA Annual Report 2019 (73 pp., no financial statements: the audited report is posted separately). In scope and extracted: GM message (2019 dividends PHP 216.4m; 53,265 gross enrolled; revenue target exceeded by 9.22% / PHP 85.7m, a printed difference not recorded as a level); Financial Highlights charts (p. 6: NOI, dividends and foreign currency generated 2018-2019 and cumulative); Enrollment Highlights (p. 7: cumulative enrolled 60,359 / 68,383, gross enrolment bars 2014-2019; 2018-2019 were already extracted; percentage changes 21.70% / 10.81% / 23.74% are derived and not recorded); SRRV options and deposits (pp. 13-14; two terms already extracted, four added; 5 May 2011 launch); 2019 scorecard (pp. 49-52: outstanding visa deposits US$548.4m, cumulative net enrolment 49,271, revenue, NOI, with targets). Out of scope: organisation, marketing events and ads, merchant-partner and facility usage counts, accreditation counts (267 marketers, 20 merchants, 43 facilities), 3,405 marketing leads, satisfaction survey (88%/56%), budget utilisation, return on marketing expense, ISO, governance, FOI requests, staff directory. The report is internally inconsistent (cumulative enrolment 68,383 vs 53,265; 2019 NOI 281.4m vs 432,746 thousand; 2019 dividend 216.4m vs 258,489 thousand; revenue target exceeded vs revenue at 48% of target); all printed versions were recorded with notes. Chart scales (p. 6) are not printed and were read as thousands (see notes). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

PRA Annual Report 2020 (64 pp., no financial statements). In scope and extracted: GM message (71.6% fall in enrolment, suspension of SRRV applications, P150M remitted for CY 2020, over US$572m deposits, net operating revenue over PHP 454m); Financial Highlights charts (p. 5: NOI 2019-2020 and cumulative, dividends 2019 and '-' for 2020, foreign currency generated 2019-2020 and cumulative); enrolled retirees 55,114 at end-2020 (already extracted) and average net enrolment 2017-2020; SRRV schemes (pp. 11-12; Expanded Courtesy terms added; SMILE/Classic/Human Touch/Courtesy deposits are the same as in the 2019 report already recorded); 2020 scorecard (pp. 41-44: outstanding deposits US$572.9m, cumulative net enrolment target, NOI, with targets). The GM's 'net operating revenue of more than PhP 454 Million' is recorded as revenue with a note (undefined, differs from the NOI on p. 42). Percentage changes are derived and not recorded. Out of scope: satisfaction survey, marketing leads (613), events and ads, accreditation counts (24 merchant partners, 96 facilities, 151 marketers), ID renewals (19,629 in 2020; 20,583 in 2019), social-integration activities, merchant/facility usage, processing-time, ISO, IT, competency measures, governance, FOI, organisation. Chart scales are not printed (see notes). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

PRA leaflet PRA-PD-LORQ-0010 (Aug 2025, 3 pp.): persons qualified (minimum age 40, spouse, children under 21, POGO/IGL workers barred), deposit tables for SRRV Classic (by age and pension) and SRRV Courtesy (foreign nationals; former Filipinos), pension proofs, documentary requirements (passport/visa, forms, medical, police, BI and NBI clearances, deposit certificate covering 3 applicants plus US$15,000 per extra dependant, relationship proof, photos), processing fee, annual fee table, processing period 30-45 working days, contacts. All amounts, ages and the processing period are now in the data (the Classic deposits, Courtesy 50+ foreign deposit, US$360 annual fee, US$1,500 processing fee and the event were already there). Validity periods of documents (6 months, 1 year, 30-day tourist visa, 90-day NBI rule) are document rules, not programme terms; not taken. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

AIMA web page "Autorização de Residência para Investimento – Art. 90.º-A" (retrieved 2 Oct 2026): regime in force since 8 Oct 2012; benefits (minimum stay 7 days in the first year, 14 days in later years; family reunification; permanent residence; naturalisation); the five current routes with minimums (10 jobs; EUR 500k research; EUR 250k culture; EUR 500k non-real-estate funds; EUR 500k company with 5/10 jobs) and document lists; family members eligible; permit valid two years; legislation list. No statistics. Standard minimums are already in the data from the laws; added the low-density reduced amounts the page prints (8 jobs, EUR 400k research, EUR 220k culture, the last inconsistent with its own 20% rule). The 2012 launch event already cites this page. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Decreto-Lei 14/2021 (4 pp.): amends arts. 3 and 90-A of Law 23/2007 under the 2020 budget authorisation: capital transfer EUR 1.5m; research, fund and company routes EUR 500k; residential real estate (subalíneas iii and iv) only in the Azores, Madeira and interior territories (Portaria 208/2017); applies to applications after entry into force; renewals and family permits of existing holders unaffected; in force 1 Jan 2022. All amounts and both dates already in the data (6 terms, 2 events). No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Decreto Regulamentar 1/2024 (45 pp.) amending Decreto Regulamentar 84/2007 after the creation of AIMA and Law 56/2023: general immigration procedures moved to AIMA, database-based proof (new art. 42-R lists minimum amounts per ARI route: 10 jobs, EUR 500k company with 5/10 jobs, EUR 500k non-real-estate funds, EUR 500k research, EUR 250k culture, restating the law), ARI articles 65-A to 65-K amended (low-density 20% only for ii, v, vi; AIMA board decides; monitoring group; biennial evaluation; procedures manual; permanent ARI), transitional rules for renewals of closed routes and fee payment deadlines (10 and 15 working days). Added one event (in force 18 Jan 2024). Amounts restate existing terms. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Decreto Regulamentar 15-A/2015 (37 pp.), amending Decreto Regulamentar 84/2007 with full republication: new arts. 65-A to 65-J regulating ARI (minimum amounts per route restating Law 63/2015; co-ownership with each owner investing the minimum; mortgages only above the minimum; promissory contract with a deposit of at least the minimum; 20% low-density reduction; five-year period counted from the grant; minimum stay 7 days in the first year and 14 days in each later two-year period; proof documents for grant and renewal; investor information desks; monitoring group meeting monthly; procedures manual); in force the day after 2 Sep 2015. Amounts are already terms (from the laws, with these conditions in their notes) and the stay rule is an event. The rest of the republication is general immigration regulation. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Law 102/2017 (74 pp.), fifth amendment to Law 23/2007 with full republication: fund route lowered to EUR 350k (Portuguese funds, 5-year maturity, 60% in Portuguese companies) and new company-capital route (EUR 350k with 5 jobs); ARI renewed for two-year periods (art. 90-A(2)); other changes on students, researchers, entrepreneurs, Blue Card. Both ARI amounts are already terms and the change is an event; the rest of the republication restates earlier ARI amounts or concerns other permits. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).
